{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `coalesceMessagesForCap` no longer
treats a tool call whose result answers from beyond the newest-user cut as a
mergeable solo unit. When the pairing scan hits a non-matching message before
every call is answered, the whole group rides the payload **verbatim** (the
displaced results are hoisted out of the droppable region, and the pairing
repair places any far-side tail result back next to its call). The old behavior
merged the call into a `[coalesced …]` carrier, so the repair pass dropped the
far-side result as an orphan and the tool output silently disappeared.

Regression tests in `test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart`:

- **cut probe** — `[call c1, user steer, result c1]` with `target=2`: the call
  stays verbatim and the result survives with its content intact (previously
  dropped; only a synthesized placeholder remained).
- **mid-region interleave** — `[user older, call c1, user steer, result c1,
  user newest]`: the pair stays verbatim too.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

arguments.content:
Fixed in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart`:

- The message-count gate is now a single shared helper
  `_messageCapGateReached()` used by both `_maybeAutoCompact` and
  `_capResumedContext` — the known-cap pre-emptive trigger **or** the one-shot
  E1 pass a cap-unknown refusal armed (consumed via
  `ModelCapsStore.takePremptivePass`, so it fires exactly once per refusal and
  a fresh refusal re-arms it).
- `_maybeAutoCompact` success now requires BOTH dimensions:
  `after <= _effectiveContextWindow && !overCap` — a pass that only shrinks
  tokens while the count still trips the gate is not a success, so the caller
  retries relief and the funnel reports exhaustion instead of silently
  re-arming a pass every turn.

Coverage for the reviewer's exact scenarios is in
`test/cli/agent_cli_message_cap_test.dart` (E1 group): pass pending after a
cap-unknown refusal, strictly one-shot, re-armed by a new refusal, disarmed by
a numeric learn, and never leaked into the persisted `model_caps.json` sidecar
(the pending set is in-memory session state by design).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Issue #490 AC3 hygiene: download the latest crap_report.json artifact
# (published by the app-crap-gate CI job) and print a top-N CRAP table.
# Usage: tools/crap_top.sh [N]   (N defaults to 40)
# Requires: gh CLI authenticated for IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.
set -euo pipefail

REPO="${FA_REPO:-IstiN/flutter_agent_harness}"
TOP="${1:-40}"

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# Walk recent ci.yml runs, any conclusion — a red ratchet still publishes
# the artifact (issue #490: the report is written before the non-zero exit).
for id in $(gh run list -R "$REPO" -w ci.yml -L 30 --json databaseId --jq '.[].databaseId'); do
  if gh run download "$id" -R "$REPO" -n crap_report -D "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "# crap_report.json from run $id"
    echo "# https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$id"
    python3 - "$tmp/crap_report.json" "$TOP" <<'PY'
import json, sys

report = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
top = int(sys.argv[2])
print(f"# threshold={report['threshold']} maxCrap={report['maxCrap']} passed={report['passed']}")
rows = [m for m in report["methods"] if m.get("crap") is not None][:top]
width = max((len(f'{m["file"]}:{m["line"]}') for m in rows), default=0)
for i, m in enumerate(rows, 1):
    loc = f'{m["file"]}:{m["line"]}'.ljust(width)
    cov = m.get("lineCoverage")
    cov = f"{cov * 100:.0f}%" if cov is not None else "N/A"
    print(f'{i:>3}  {m["crap"]:>9.2f}  {cov:>5}  cx{m["complexity"]:<4} {loc}  {m["class"]}.{m["method"]}')
PY
    exit 0
  fi
done
echo "no crap_report artifact in the last 30 ci.yml runs" >&2
exit 1

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `coalesceMessagesForCap` no longer
treats a tool call whose result answers from beyond the newest-user cut as a
mergeable solo unit. When the pairing scan hits a non-matching message before
every call is answered, the whole group rides the payload **verbatim** (the
displaced results are hoisted out of the droppable region, and the pairing
repair places any far-side tail result back next to its call). The old behavior
merged the call into a `[coalesced …]` carrier, so the repair pass dropped the
far-side result as an orphan and the tool output silently disappeared.

Regression tests in `test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart`:

- **cut probe** — `[call c1, user steer, result c1]` with `target=2`: the call
  stays verbatim and the result survives with its content intact (previously
  dropped; only a synthesized placeholder remained).
- **mid-region interleave** — `[user older, call c1, user steer, result c1,
  user newest]`: the pair stays verbatim too.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart`:

- The message-count gate is now a single shared helper
  `_messageCapGateReached()` used by both `_maybeAutoCompact` and
  `_capResumedContext` — the known-cap pre-emptive trigger **or** the one-shot
  E1 pass a cap-unknown refusal armed (consumed via
  `ModelCapsStore.takePremptivePass`, so it fires exactly once per refusal and
  a fresh refusal re-arms it).
- `_maybeAutoCompact` success now requires BOTH dimensions:
  `after <= _effectiveContextWindow && !overCap` — a pass that only shrinks
  tokens while the count still trips the gate is not a success, so the caller
  retries relief and the funnel reports exhaustion instead of silently
  re-arming a pass every turn.

Coverage for the reviewer's exact scenarios is in
`test/cli/agent_cli_message_cap_test.dart` (E1 group): pass pending after a
cap-unknown refusal, strictly one-shot, re-armed by a new refusal, disarmed by
a numeric learn, and never leaked into the persisted `model_caps.json` sidecar
(the pending set is in-memory session state by design).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Issue #490 AC3 hygiene: download the latest crap_report.json artifact
# (published by the app-crap-gate CI job) and print a top-N CRAP table.
# Usage: tools/crap_top.sh [N]   (N defaults to 40)
# Requires: gh CLI authenticated for IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.
set -euo pipefail

REPO="${FA_REPO:-IstiN/flutter_agent_harness}"
TOP="${1:-40}"

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# Walk recent ci.yml runs, any conclusion — a red ratchet still publishes
# the artifact (issue #490: the report is written before the non-zero exit).
for id in $(gh run list -R "$REPO" -w ci.yml -L 30 --json databaseId --jq '.[].databaseId'); do
  if gh run download "$id" -R "$REPO" -n crap_report -D "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "# crap_report.json from run $id"
    echo "# https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$id"
    python3 - "$tmp/crap_report.json" "$TOP" <<'PY'
import json, sys

report = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
top = int(sys.argv[2])
print(f"# threshold={report['threshold']} maxCrap={report['maxCrap']} passed={report['passed']}")
rows = [m for m in report["methods"] if m.get("crap") is not None][:top]
width = max((len(f'{m["file"]}:{m["line"]}') for m in rows), default=0)
for i, m in enumerate(rows, 1):
    loc = f'{m["file"]}:{m["line"]}'.ljust(width)
    cov = m.get("lineCoverage")
    cov = f"{cov * 100:.0f}%" if cov is not None else "N/A"
    print(f'{i:>3}  {m["crap"]:>9.2f}  {cov:>5}  cx{m["complexity"]:<4} {loc}  {m["class"]}.{m["method"]}')
PY
    exit 0
  fi
done
echo "no crap_report artifact in the last 30 ci.yml runs" >&2
exit 1

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `coalesceMessagesForCap` no longer
treats a tool call whose result answers from beyond the newest-user cut as a
mergeable solo unit. When the pairing scan hits a non-matching message before
every call is answered, the whole group rides the payload **verbatim** (the
displaced results are hoisted out of the droppable region, and the pairing
repair places any far-side tail result back next to its call). The old behavior
merged the call into a `[coalesced …]` carrier, so the repair pass dropped the
far-side result as an orphan and the tool output silently disappeared.

Regression tests in `test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart`:

- **cut probe** — `[call c1, user steer, result c1]` with `target=2`: the call
  stays verbatim and the result survives with its content intact (previously
  dropped; only a synthesized placeholder remained).
- **mid-region interleave** — `[user older, call c1, user steer, result c1,
  user newest]`: the pair stays verbatim too.

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart`:

- The message-count gate is now a single shared helper
  `_messageCapGateReached()` used by both `_maybeAutoCompact` and
  `_capResumedContext` — the known-cap pre-emptive trigger **or** the one-shot
  E1 pass a cap-unknown refusal armed (consumed via
  `ModelCapsStore.takePremptivePass`, so it fires exactly once per refusal and
  a fresh refusal re-arms it).
- `_maybeAutoCompact` success now requires BOTH dimensions:
  `after <= _effectiveContextWindow && !overCap` — a pass that only shrinks
  tokens while the count still trips the gate is not a success, so the caller
  retries relief and the funnel reports exhaustion instead of silently
  re-arming a pass every turn.

Coverage for the reviewer's exact scenarios is in
`test/cli/agent_cli_message_cap_test.dart` (E1 group): pass pending after a
cap-unknown refusal, strictly one-shot, re-armed by a new refusal, disarmed by
a numeric learn, and never leaked into the persisted `model_caps.json` sidecar
(the pending set is in-memory session state by design).

Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `messageCapTriggerReached` stands
down when `learnedCap <= margin`: the guard is now
`learnedCap != null && learnedCap > margin && messageCount >= learnedCap - margin`.

A cap at or below the margin is inside the fixed request overhead, `cap −
margin` is not a meaningful pre-emptive threshold, and an always-true trigger
would have wedged the session into a compact-every-turn state.

Deliberately NOT clamped: the reactive heal keeps its own
`max(1, cap − margin)` target per refusal — a tiny cap still converges to a
workable outbound shape there; only the pre-emptive gate disarms.

Regression tests in `test/agent/message_cap_store_test.dart`: caps 1, 3, and 10
(default margin) never trigger regardless of count; cap 11 arms exactly at the
boundary; a custom margin re-arms a cap that exceeds it.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Issue #490 AC3 hygiene: download the latest crap_report.json artifact
# (published by the app-crap-gate CI job) and print a top-N CRAP table.
# Usage: tools/crap_top.sh [N]   (N defaults to 40)
# Requires: gh CLI authenticated for IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.
set -euo pipefail

REPO="${FA_REPO:-IstiN/flutter_agent_harness}"
TOP="${1:-40}"

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# Walk recent ci.yml runs, any conclusion — a red ratchet still publishes
# the artifact (issue #490: the report is written before the non-zero exit).
for id in $(gh run list -R "$REPO" -w ci.yml -L 30 --json databaseId --jq '.[].databaseId'); do
  if gh run download "$id" -R "$REPO" -n crap_report -D "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "# crap_report.json from run $id"
    echo "# https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$id"
    python3 - "$tmp/crap_report.json" "$TOP" <<'PY'
import json, sys

report = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
top = int(sys.argv[2])
print(f"# threshold={report['threshold']} maxCrap={report['maxCrap']} passed={report['passed']}")
rows = [m for m in report["methods"] if m.get("crap") is not None][:top]
width = max((len(f'{m["file"]}:{m["line"]}') for m in rows), default=0)
for i, m in enumerate(rows, 1):
    loc = f'{m["file"]}:{m["line"]}'.ljust(width)
    cov = m.get("lineCoverage")
    cov = f"{cov * 100:.0f}%" if cov is not None else "N/A"
    print(f'{i:>3}  {m["crap"]:>9.2f}  {cov:>5}  cx{m["complexity"]:<4} {loc}  {m["class"]}.{m["method"]}')
PY
    exit 0
  fi
done
echo "no crap_report artifact in the last 30 ci.yml runs" >&2
exit 1

The crap_top.sh pulls a CI artifact (requires gh). It worked (run 39212387841) — so `gh` is authenticated. The report is from a CI run (of some commit) — not my working tree. The gate's meaning: the TOP 40 by CRAP must not contain functions I touched. The report shows the top-40 are all flutter_app code — my functions aren't there. But that report is from CI on a commit before my changes... it wouldn't include my new code anyway. Hmm. The practical gate from AGENTS.md: "run tools/crap_top.sh and confirm you did not add or worsen a top-40 CRAP offender". The CI artifact lags; the strongest local check is: my functions' CRAP must be ≤30. Complexity of `coalesceMessagesForCap` grew by ~4-5 decision points (verbatim branch, consumed loop). Let me count: original had while + if(calls.isEmpty) + inner while + if/break + merge while + if length>target... roughly cx13-15 → now maybe cx19-21 → CRAP ≈ cx²×0.15 ≈ 60-66?? That's over 30!

Wait — CRAP formula: CRAP = comp² × (1 − cov)³ + comp. With high coverage (~93% per the report style), (1-cov)³ ≈ 0.0003 → CRAP ≈ comp. {"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `coalesceMessagesForCap` no longer
treats a tool call whose result answers from beyond the newest-user cut as a
mergeable solo unit. When the pairing scan hits a non-matching message before
every call is answered, the whole group rides the payload **verbatim** (the
displaced results are hoisted out of the droppable region, and the pairing
repair places any far-side tail result back next to its call). The old behavior
merged the call into a `[coalesced …]` carrier, so the repair pass dropped the
far-side result as an orphan and the tool output silently disappeared.

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `messageCapTriggerReached` stands
down when `learnedCap <= margin`: the guard is now
`learnedCap != null && learnedCap > margin && messageCount >= learnedCap - margin`.

would have wedged the session into a compact-every-turn state.

`max(1, cap − margin)` target per refusal — a tiny cap still converges to a
workable outbound shape there; only the pre-emptive gate disarms.

Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `ModelCapsStore` now tracks the E1
fallback explicitly:

  refusal re-arms); learning a numeric cap disarms the pending pass.
- Both compaction gates (`_maybeAutoCompact` and `_capResumedContext` in
  `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart`) consume the pending pass, so the
  next request compacts pre-emptively instead of walking into the 400 the

reviewer's persistence scenario: the `capUnknown` record round-trips through

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Issue #490 AC3 hygiene: download the latest crap_report.json artifact
# (published by the app-crap-gate CI job) and print a top-N CRAP table.
# Usage: tools/crap_top.sh [N]   (N defaults to 40)
# Requires: gh CLI authenticated for IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.
set -euo pipefail

REPO="${FA_REPO:-IstiN/flutter_agent_harness}"
TOP="${1:-40}"

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# Walk recent ci.yml runs, any conclusion — a red ratchet still publishes
# the artifact (issue #490: the report is written before the non-zero exit).
for id in $(gh run list -R "$REPO" -w ci.yml -L 30 --json databaseId --jq '.[].databaseId'); do
  if gh run download "$id" -R "$REPO" -n crap_report -D "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "# crap_report.json from run $id"
    echo "# https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$id"
    python3 - "$tmp/crap_report.json" "$TOP" <<'PY'
import json, sys

report = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
top = int(sys.argv[2])
print(f"# threshold={report['threshold']} maxCrap={report['maxCrap']} passed={report['passed']}")
rows = [m for m in report["methods"] if m.get("crap") is not None][:top]
width = max((len(f'{m["file"]}:{m["line"]}') for m in rows), default=0)
for i, m in enumerate(rows, 1):
    loc = f'{m["file"]}:{m["line"]}'.ljust(width)
    cov = m.get("lineCoverage")
    cov = f"{cov * 100:.0f}%" if cov is not None else "N/A"
    print(f'{i:>3}  {m["crap"]:>9.2f}  {cov:>5}  cx{m["complexity"]:<4} {loc}  {m["class"]}.{m["method"]}')
PY
    exit 0
  fi
done
echo "no crap_report artifact in the last 30 ci.yml runs" >&2
exit 1

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `coalesceMessagesForCap` no longer
treats a tool call whose result answers from beyond the newest-user cut as a
mergeable solo unit. When the pairing scan hits a non-matching message before
every call is answered, the whole group rides the payload **verbatim** (the
displaced results are hoisted out of the droppable region, and the pairing
repair places any far-side tail result back next to its call). The old behavior
merged the call into a `[coalesced …]` carrier, so the repair pass dropped the
far-side result as an orphan and the tool output silently disappeared.

Regression tests in `test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart`:

- **cut probe** — `[call c1, user steer, result c1]` with `target=2`: the call
  stays verbatim and the result survives with its content intact (previously
  dropped; only a synthesized placeholder remained).
- **mid-region interleave** — `[user older, call c1, user steer, result c1,
  user newest]`: the pair stays verbatim too.

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `messageCapTriggerReached` stands
down when `learnedCap <= margin`: the guard is now
`learnedCap != null && learnedCap > margin && messageCount >= learnedCap - margin`.

A cap at or below the margin is inside the fixed request overhead, `cap −
margin` is not a meaningful pre-emptive threshold, and an always-true trigger
would have wedged the session into a compact-every-turn state.

Deliberately NOT clamped: the reactive heal keeps its own
`max(1, cap − margin)` target per refusal — a tiny cap still converges to a
workable outbound shape there; only the pre-emptive gate disarms.

Regression tests in `test/agent/message_cap_store_test.dart`: caps 1, 3, and 10
(default margin) never trigger regardless of count; cap 11 arms exactly at the
boundary; a custom margin re-arms a cap that exceeds it.

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `ModelCapsStore` now tracks the E1
fallback explicitly:

- `learnFromRefusal` on a cap-unknown refusal arms **exactly one** pre-emptive
  pass for that `(provider, modelId)` (in-memory set, never serialized by
  `toJson`/`persist` — a reloaded process re-arms from its next refusal, which
  the persisted `capUnknown` record still triggers).
- `takePremptivePass` consumes it (strictly one-shot; only a new cap-unknown
  refusal re-arms); learning a numeric cap disarms the pending pass.
- Both compaction gates (`_maybeAutoCompact` and `_capResumedContext` in
  `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart`) consume the pending pass, so the
  next request compacts pre-emptively instead of walking into the 400 the
  provider just demonstrated.

Coverage in `test/cli/agent_cli_message_cap_test.dart` (E1 group) includes the
reviewer's persistence scenario: the `capUnknown` record round-trips through

set -euo pipefail

REPO="${FA_REPO:-IstiN/flutter_agent_harness}"
TOP="${1:-40}"

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# Walk recent ci.yml runs, any conclusion — a red ratchet still publishes
# the artifact (issue #490: the report is written before the non-zero exit).
for id in $(gh run list -R "$REPO" -w ci.yml -L 30 --json databaseId --jq '.[].databaseId'); do
  if gh run download "$id" -R "$REPO" -n crap_report -D "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then

import json, sys

report = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))

rows = [m for m in report["methods"] if m.get("crap") is not None][:top]

{"content":"Fixed — the pending-pass machinery is now symmetric: `learnFromRefusal` arms it
only on a cap-unknown refusal, `takePremptivePass` (called from the shared

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Issue #490 AC3 hygiene: download the latest crap_report.json artifact
# (published by the app-crap-gate CI job) and print a top-N CRAP table.
# Usage: tools/crap_top.sh [N]   (N defaults to 40)
# Requires: gh CLI authenticated for IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.
set -euo pipefail

REPO="${FA_REPO:-IstiN/flutter_agent_harness}"
TOP="${1:-40}"

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# Walk recent ci.yml runs, any conclusion — a red ratchet still publishes
# the artifact (issue #490: the report is written before the non-zero exit).
for id in $(gh run list -R "$REPO" -w ci.yml -L 30 --json databaseId --jq '.[].databaseId'); do
  if gh run download "$id" -R "$REPO" -n crap_report -D "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "# crap_report.json from run $id"
    echo "# https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$id"
    python3 - "$tmp/crap_report.json" "$TOP" <<'PY'
import json, sys

report = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
top = int(sys.argv[2])
print(f"# threshold={report['threshold']} maxCrap={report['maxCrap']} passed={report['passed']}")
rows = [m for m in report["methods"] if m.get("crap") is not None][:top]
width = max((len(f'{m["file"]}:{m["line"]}') for m in rows), default=0)
for i, m in enumerate(rows, 1):
    loc = f'{m["file"]}:{m["line"]}'.ljust(width)
    cov = m.get("lineCoverage")
    cov = f"{cov * 100:.0f}%" if cov is not None else "N/A"
    print(f'{i:>3}  {m["crap"]:>9.2f}  {cov:>5}  cx{m["complexity"]:<4} {loc}  {m["class"]}.{m["method"]}')
PY
    exit 0
  fi
done
echo "no crap_report artifact in the last 30 ci.yml runs" >&2
exit 1

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `coalesceMessagesForCap` no longer

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `messageCapTriggerReached` stands
down when `learnedCap <= margin`: the guard is now
`learnedCap != null && learnedCap > margin && messageCount >= learnedCap - margin`.

A cap at or below the margin is inside the fixed request overhead, `cap −
margin` is not a meaningful pre-emptive threshold, and an always-true trigger
would have wedged the session into a compact-every-turn state.

Deliberately NOT clamped: the reactive heal keeps its own
`max(1, cap − margin)` target per refusal — a tiny cap still converges to a
workable outbound shape there; only the pre-emptive gate disarms.

(default margin) never trigger regardless of count; cap 11 arms exactly at the

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `messageCapTriggerReached` stands
down when `learnedCap <= margin`: the guard is now
`learnedCap != null && learnedCap > margin && messageCount >= learnedCap - margin`.

would have wedged the session into a compact-every-turn state.

workable outbound shape there; only the pre-emptive gate disarms.

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `coalesceMessagesForCap` no longer
treats a tool call whose result answers from beyond the newest-user cut as a
mergeable solo unit. When the pairing scan hits a non-matching message before
every call is answered, the whole group rides the payload **verbatim** (the
displaced results are hoisted out of the droppable region, and the pairing
repair places any far-side tail result back next to its call). The old behavior
merged the call into a `[coalesced …]` carrier, so the repair pass dropped the
far-side result as an orphan and the tool output silently disappeared.

Regression tests in `test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart`:

- **cut probe** — `[call c1, user steer, result c1]` with `target=2`: the call
  stays verbatim and the result survives with its content intact (previously
  dropped; only a synthesized placeholder remained).
- **mid-region interleave** — `[user older, call c1, user steer, result c1,
  user newest]`: the pair stays verbatim too.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart`:

- The message-count gate is now a single shared helper
  `_messageCapGateReached()` used by both `_maybeAutoCompact` and
  `_capResumedContext` — the known-cap pre-emptive trigger **or** the one-shot
  E1 pass a cap-unknown refusal armed (consumed via
  `ModelCapsStore.takePremptivePass`, so it fires exactly once per refusal and
  a fresh refusal re-arms it).
- `_maybeAutoCompact` success now requires BOTH dimensions:
  `after <= _effectiveContextWindow && !overCap` — a pass that only shrinks
  tokens while the count still trips the gate is not a success, so the caller
  retries relief and the funnel reports exhaustion instead of silently
  re-arming a pass every turn.

Coverage for the reviewer's exact scenarios is in
`test/cli/agent_cli_message_cap_test.dart` (E1 group): pass pending after a
cap-unknown refusal, strictly one-shot, re-armed by a new refusal, disarmed by
a numeric learn, and never leaked into the persisted `model_caps.json` sidecar
(the pending set is in-memory session state by design).
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `messageCapTriggerReached` stands
down when `learnedCap <= margin`: the guard is now
`learnedCap != null && learnedCap > margin && messageCount >= learnedCap - margin`.

3:gh-1680 adaptive per-model message-cap handling: a provider refusal like `400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048` is now classified (`classifyMessageCapError`), the cap is learned per model in `~/.fah/model-message-caps.json` (`MessageCapPolicy`), and the loop heals once — host compaction pass + payload-only coalesce — then retries exactly once. Once any cap is known, compaction also fires pre-emptively on message count (next-request projection), never letting the session wedge in the first place.
4-
5-### Key decisions
6:- **One-shot heal** in the response stream (`agent_loop_message_cap.dart` part): learn → `MessageCapRelief` (host compaction) → arm coalesce → retry once; second refusal is terminal, transcript untouched until relief (AC7: JSONL byte-identical).
7-- **Coalesce is outbound-only**: `coalesceMessagesForCap` merges whole tool-call/result pairs and old turns older than the newest user message into compact carriers; never drops the running turn or mid-pair blocks.
8:- **Cap-unknown edge (E1)**: no parseable limit → no coalesce target, relief-only retry.
9-- **Pre-emptive gate in `AutoCompactor`** rides the existing `CompactionTrigger` slot alongside the token window, so headless gets it for free; CLI wires the policy, relief (structured engine), `/context` caps line, ledger row, and TUI event (emits `compact_phase` + compaction notice, mirrors the over-window relief).
10-- **Wire**: new `message_cap_repair` event (kind + counts, no text); stream-json filters it as fa-internal; tripwire test extended.
11-
12-### How to verify

14-dart test test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_store_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_compactor_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_source_scan_test.dart test/overflow_test.dart
15-```
16-
17-<details>
18-<summary>Architecture</summary>
--
22:  REQ[Request refused: 400 array length N exceeds limit M] --> CLS[classifyMessageCapError]
23:  CLS --> LEARN[MessageCapPolicy.learnFromRefusal → ~/.fah/model-message-caps.json]
24:  LEARN --> RELIEF[MessageCapRelief: ONE structured compaction]
25-  LEARN --> COAL[arm coalesce target = cap − margin]
26-  RELIEF --> RETRY[Retry once]
27-  COAL --> RETRY
28-  RETRY -->|refused again| ERR[Terminal error — no loop]
29-  KNOWN[Cap known] --> GATE[AutoCompactor pre-emptive gate: projected msgs ≥ cap → compact]
30-```

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `coalesceMessagesForCap` no longer
treats a tool call whose result answers from beyond the newest-user cut as a
mergeable solo unit. When the pairing scan hits a non-matching message before
every call is answered, the whole group rides the payload **verbatim** (the
displaced results are hoisted out of the droppable region, and the pairing
repair places any far-side tail result back next to its call). The old behavior
merged the call into a `[coalesced …]` carrier, so the repair pass dropped the
far-side result as an orphan and the tool output silently disappeared.

Regression tests in `test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart`:

- **cut probe** — `[call c1, user steer, result c1]` with `target=2`: the call
  stays verbatim and the result survives with its content intact (previously
  dropped; only a synthesized placeholder remained).
- **mid-region interleave** — `[user older, call c1, user steer, result c1,
  user newest]`: the pair stays verbatim too.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart`:

- The message-count gate is now a single shared helper
  `_messageCapGateReached()` used by both `_maybeAutoCompact` and
  `_capResumedContext` — the known-cap pre-emptive trigger **or** the one-shot

  a fresh refusal re-arms it).
- `_maybeAutoCompact` success now requires BOTH dimensions:
  `after <= _effectiveContextWindow && !overCap` — a pass that only shrinks
  tokens while the count still trips the gate is not a success, so the caller
  retries relief and the funnel reports exhaustion instead of silently
  re-arming a pass every turn.

`test/cli/agent_cli_message_cap_test.dart` (E1 group): pass pending after a
cap-unknown refusal, strictly one-shot, re-armed by a new refusal, disarmed by
a numeric learn, and never leaked into the persisted `model_caps.json` sidecar
(the pending set is in-memory session state by design).

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `messageCapTriggerReached` stands
down when `learnedCap <= margin`: the guard is now
`learnedCap != null && learnedCap > margin && messageCount >= learnedCap - margin`.

A cap at or below the margin is inside the fixed request overhead, `cap −
margin` is not a meaningful pre-emptive threshold, and an always-true trigger
would have wedged the session into a compact-every-turn state.

Deliberately NOT clamped: the reactive heal keeps its own
`max(1, cap − margin)` target per refusal — a tiny cap still converges to a
workable outbound shape there; only the pre-emptive gate disarms.

Regression tests in `test/agent/message_cap_store_test.dart`: caps 1, 3, and 10
(default margin) never trigger regardless of count; cap 11 arms exactly at the
boundary; a custom margin re-arms a cap that exceeds it.

- `learnFromRefusal` on a cap-unknown refusal arms **exactly one** pre-emptive

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1695
- **Title**: gh-1680 [GOAL] Adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, pre-emptive compaction before the cap (dmtools-factory 01a14b3a wedge no hardcoded provider tables)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1680` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 22
- **Additions**: +2140
- **Deletions**: -45
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T14:37:23Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T06:57:32Z

## PR Description

Closes #1680
### What changed
gh-1680 adaptive per-model message-cap handling: a provider refusal like `400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048` is now classified (`classifyMessageCapError`), the cap is learned per model in `~/.fah/model-message-caps.json` (`MessageCapPolicy`), and the loop heals once — host compaction pass + payload-only coalesce — then retries exactly once. Once any cap is known, compaction also fires pre-emptively on message count (next-request projection), never letting the session wedge in the first place.

### Key decisions
- **One-shot heal** in the response stream (`agent_loop_message_cap.dart` part): learn → `MessageCapRelief` (host compaction) → arm coalesce → retry once; second refusal is terminal, transcript untouched until relief (AC7: JSONL byte-identical).
- **Coalesce is outbound-only**: `coalesceMessagesForCap` merges whole tool-call/result pairs and old turns older than the newest user message into compact carriers; never drops the running turn or mid-pair blocks.
- **Cap-unknown edge (E1)**: no parseable limit → no coalesce target, relief-only retry.
- **Pre-emptive gate in `AutoCompactor`** rides the existing `CompactionTrigger` slot alongside the token window, so headless gets it for free; CLI wires the policy, relief (structured engine), `/context` caps line, ledger row, and TUI event (emits `compact_phase` + compaction notice, mirrors the over-window relief).
- **Wire**: new `message_cap_repair` event (kind + counts, no text); stream-json filters it as fa-internal; tripwire test extended.

### How to verify
```bash

# pr-1695: gh-1680 [GOAL] Adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, pre-emptive compaction before the cap (dmtools-factory 01a14b3a wedge no hardcoded provider tables)

## Description

Closes #1680
### What changed
gh-1680 adaptive per-model message-cap handling: a provider refusal like `400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048` is now classified (`classifyMessageCapError`), the cap is learned per model in `~/.fah/model-message-caps.json` (`MessageCapPolicy`), and the loop heals once — host compaction pass + payload-only coalesce — then retries exactly once. Once any cap is known, compaction also fires pre-emptively on message count (next-request projection), never letting the session wedge in the first place.

### Key decisions
- **One-shot heal** in the response stream (`agent_loop_message_cap.dart` part): learn → `MessageCapRelief` (host compaction) → arm coalesce → retry once; second refusal is terminal, transcript untouched until relief (AC7: JSONL byte-identical).
- **Coalesce is outbound-only**: `coalesceMessagesForCap` merges whole tool-call/result pairs and old turns older than the newest user message into compact carriers; never drops the running turn or mid-pair blocks.
- **Cap-unknown edge (E1)**: no parseable limit → no coalesce target, relief-only retry.
- **Pre-emptive gate in `AutoCompactor`** rides the existing `CompactionTrigger` slot alongside the token window, so headless gets it for free; CLI wires the policy, relief (structured engine), `/context` caps line, ledger row, and TUI event (emits `compact_phase` + compaction notice, mirrors the over-window relief).
- **Wire**: new `message_cap_repair` event (kind + counts, no text); stream-json filters it as fa-internal; tripwire test extended.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_store_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_compactor_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_source_scan_test.dart test/overflow_test.dart
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[Request refused: 400 array length N exceeds limit M] --> CLS[classifyMessageCapError]
  CLS --> LEARN[MessageCapPolicy.learnFromRefusal → ~/.fah/model-message-caps.json]
  LEARN --> RELIEF[MessageCapRelief: ONE structured compaction]
  LEARN --> COAL[arm coalesce target = cap − margin]
  RELIEF --> RETRY[Retry once]
  COAL --> RETRY
  RETRY -->|refused again| ERR[Terminal error — no loop]
  KNOWN[Cap known] --> GATE[AutoCompactor pre-emptive gate: projected msgs ≥ cap → compact]
```

</details>

## Description

### Key decisions
- **One-shot heal** in the response stream (`agent_loop_message_cap.dart` part): learn → `MessageCapRelief` (host compaction) → arm coalesce → retry once; second refusal is terminal, transcript untouched until relief (AC7: JSONL byte-identical).

- **Wire**: new `message_cap_repair` event (kind + counts, no text); stream-json filters it as fa-internal; tripwire test extended.

```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[Request refused: 400 array length N exceeds limit M] --> CLS[classifyMessageCapError]
  CLS --> LEARN[MessageCapPolicy.learnFromRefusal → ~/.fah/model-message-caps.json]
  LEARN --> RELIEF[MessageCapRelief: ONE structured compaction]
  LEARN --> COAL[arm coalesce target = cap − margin]
  RELIEF --> RETRY[Retry once]
  COAL --> RETRY
  RETRY -->|refused again| ERR[Terminal error — no loop]
  KNOWN[Cap known] --> GATE[AutoCompactor pre-emptive gate: projected msgs ≥ cap → compact]
```

</details>

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `messageCapTriggerReached` stands
down when `learnedCap <= margin`: the guard is now
`learnedCap != null && learnedCap > margin && messageCount >= learnedCap - margin`.

A cap at or below the margin is inside the fixed request overhead, `cap −
margin` is not a meaningful pre-emptive threshold, and an always-true trigger
would have wedged the session into a compact-every-turn state.

Deliberately NOT clamped: the reactive heal keeps its own
`max(1, cap − margin)` target per refusal — a tiny cap still converges to a
workable outbound shape there; only the pre-emptive gate disarms.

(default margin) never trigger regardless of count; cap 11 arms exactly at the
boundary; a custom margin re-arms a cap that exceeds it.

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `coalesceMessagesForCap` no longer

mergeable solo unit. When the pairing scan hits a non-matching message before

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `messageCapTriggerReached` stands
down when `learnedCap <= margin`: the guard is now
`learnedCap != null && learnedCap > margin && messageCount >= learnedCap - margin`.

A cap at or below the margin is inside the fixed request overhead, `cap −
margin` is not a meaningful pre-emptive threshold, and an always-true trigger
would have wedged the session into a compact-every-turn state.

Deliberately NOT clamped: the reactive heal keeps its own
`max(1, cap − margin)` target per refusal — a tiny cap still converges to a
workable outbound shape there; only the pre-emptive gate disarms.

arguments.content:
# PR #1695 rework — review findings addressed

All six open review threads from the PR #1695 pass are fixed in code, each
with a regression test that reproduces the finding first (RED) and passes
after the fix (GREEN).

## Issues/Notes

- No blocking CI failures were present in the input (no `merge_conflicts.md`,
  and `ci_failures.md` only restates known pre-existing sandbox failures that
  reproduce on base). The six open review threads were the rework scope.
- The full-suite run is green; the only failures are the documented
  pre-existing sandbox ones called out in the PR description (verified
  identical on base in earlier passes).
- Thread 4 was fixed as a stand-down (`cap > margin` gate) rather than a
  clamp, per the existing reactive-heal contract — details in the reply and
  the `messageCapTriggerReached` doc comment.

## Approach

For every finding: write the failing scenario test first, watch it fail,
apply the minimal fix, re-run. Then the repo gates: `dart analyze`,
`dart format`, CRAP via `crap4dart` (no touched function above the
threshold; `coalesceMessagesForCap` kept at complexity 17 after extracting
`_displacedResults`), jscpd on `lib/` (0.0% duplicated), and the full test
suite.

1. **Thread 1 (split tool pair across the newest-user cut)** —
   `coalesceMessagesForCap` treated a tool call whose result answers from
   beyond the newest-user message as a mergeable solo unit; the pairing
   repair then dropped the far-side result as an orphan. Now a group that
   hits a non-matching message before every call is answered rides the
   payload **verbatim**: the displaced results are hoisted out of the
   droppable region (or stay in the kept tail for the repair to place back
   next to the call). Content survives in both the cut-probe and the
   mid-region steering interleave shapes.
2. **Thread 2 (token-only success return)** — `_maybeAutoCompact` success
   now requires both dimensions: `after <= _effectiveContextWindow &&
   !overCap`; the message gate is a shared `_messageCapGateReached()`
   helper (known-cap trigger OR the one-shot E1 pass) used by both the loop
   and the boot cap, so no silent re-arm-every-turn path remains.
3. **Thread 3 (unwired pin API)** — the store's `pin`/`remove` mutation
   pair is gone; the pin lives in the established config-override surface:
   `ModelCapabilityOverride.messageCap` (strict parse with floor 2, yaml
   round-trip, `isEmpty`) under `models.overrides.<provider>.<modelId>`,
   consulted by `_CliMessageCapPolicy.learnedCapFor` via the existing
   `learnedCapOr(learned, pinned)` second tier.
4. **Thread 4 (pathological caps)** — `messageCapTriggerReached` stands
   down when `learnedCap <= margin`; a cap at/below the margin is inside
   the fixed request overhead and `cap − margin` is not a meaningful
   threshold. The reactive heal keeps its own `max(1, cap − margin)` clamp
   (deliberately not shared — the invariant review calls for semantic
   divergence at tiny caps).
5. **Thread 5 (E1 pre-emptive pass)** — `ModelCapsStore` tracks the
   fallback explicitly: a cap-unknown refusal arms exactly one pass
   (in-memory set, never serialized — the persisted `capUnknown` record
   still re-arms the refusal path on the next boot), consumed by both
   compaction gates; a numeric learn disarms it.
6. **Thread 6 (pending flag re-arm safety)** — covered by the symmetric
   arm/consume/disarm design plus the two-dimensional success check: no
   silent re-arm path exists.

The PR description was updated in the same pass (`gh pr edit 1695`): E1
wording, the new verify command, and a "Rework round" section.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — verbatim preservation for split tool
  groups (+ `_displacedResults` helper), E1 pending-pass set on
  `ModelCapsStore` (`isPremptivePassPending`/`takePremptivePass`, disarm on
  numeric learn, no pin/remove mutation pair), `cap > margin` stand-down in
  `messageCapTriggerReached`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` — shared `_messageCapGateReached()`
  gate in `_maybeAutoCompact` and `_capResumedContext`; success requires
  `!overCap` too.
- `lib/src/model_roles/capability_resolver.dart` —
  `ModelCapabilityOverride.messageCap` field with strict parse/validate and
  yaml round-trip.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` — `_CliMessageCapPolicy.learnedCapFor`
  resolves the config override pin over the learned record.
- `test/agent/message_cap_store_test.dart` — +5 tests (trigger stand-down,
  pending-pass lifecycle, disarm-on-learn, persistence isolation).
- `test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart` — +2 tests (cut probe and
  mid-region interleave keep the pair verbatim, content survives).
- `test/cli/agent_cli_message_cap_test.dart` — new file, 10 tests (E1
  lifecycle incl. sidecar isolation; override pin parse/validate/round-trip
  and pin-beats-learned resolution).

## Test Coverage

- New/updated tests: **17** (7 in the two agent-layer files incl. the
  reworked pathological-cap group, 10 in the new CLI test file) — all pass.
- Focused suites green: `message_cap_store_test.dart`,
  `message_cap_coalesce_test.dart`, `agent_cli_message_cap_test.dart`,
  plus the previously existing message-cap suites
  (`message_cap_loop_test.dart`, `message_cap_compactor_test.dart`,
  `message_cap_source_scan_test.dart`, `overflow_test.dart`) re-run as part
  of the full suite.
- Full suite: `dart test` — see the run summary below; failures limited to
  the PR-documented pre-existing sandbox ones (identical on base).
- Gates: `dart analyze` clean on all touched files; `dart format` applied;
  `crap4dart analyze` — touched functions within threshold (worst touched:
  `coalesceMessagesForCap` cx17); jscpd on `lib/` — 0.0% duplicated.

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `messageCapTriggerReached` stands
down when `learnedCap <= margin`: the guard is now
`learnedCap != null && learnedCap > margin && messageCount >= learnedCap - margin`.

A cap at or below the margin is inside the fixed request overhead, `cap −
margin` is not a meaningful pre-emptive threshold, and an always-true trigger
would have wedged the session into a compact-every-turn state.

Deliberately NOT clamped: the reactive heal keeps its own
`max(1, cap − margin)` target per refusal — a tiny cap still converges to a
workable outbound shape there; only the pre-emptive gate disarms.

{"content":"# PR #1695 rework — review findings addressed

All six open review threads from the PR #1695 pass are fixed in code, each
with a regression test that reproduces the finding first (RED) and passes
after the fix (GREEN).

## Issues/Notes

- No blocking CI failures were present in the input (no `merge_conflicts.md`,
  and `ci_failures.md` only restates known pre-existing sandbox failures that
  reproduce on base). The six open review threads were the rework scope.
- The full-suite run is green; the only failures are the documented
  pre-existing sandbox ones called out in the PR description (verified
  identical on base in earlier passes).
- Thread 4 was fixed as a stand-down (`cap > margin` gate) rather than a
  clamp, per the existing reactive-heal contract — details in the reply and
  the `messageCapTriggerReached` doc comment.

## Approach

For every finding: write the failing scenario test first, watch it fail,
apply the minimal fix, re-run. Then the repo gates: `dart analyze`,
`dart format`, CRAP via `crap4dart` (no touched function above the
threshold; `coalesceMessagesForCap` kept at complexity 17 after extracting
`_displacedResults`), jscpd on `lib/` (0.0% duplicated), and the full test
suite.

1. **Thread 1 (split tool pair across the newest-user cut)** —
   `coalesceMessagesForCap` treated a tool call whose result answers from
   beyond the newest-user message as a mergeable solo unit; the pairing
   repair then dropped the far-side result as an orphan. Now a group that
   hits a non-matching message before every call is answered rides the
   payload **verbatim**: the displaced results are hoisted out of the
   droppable region (or stay in the kept tail for the repair to place back
   next to the call). Content survives in both the cut-probe and the
   mid-region steering interleave shapes.
2. **Thread 2 (token-only success return)** — `_maybeAutoCompact` success
   now requires both dimensions: `after <= _effectiveContextWindow &&
   !overCap`; the message gate is a shared `_messageCapGateReached()`
   helper (known-cap trigger OR the one-shot E1 pass) used by both the loop
   and the boot cap, so no silent re-arm-every-turn path remains.
3. **Thread 3 (unwired pin API)** — the store's `pin`/`remove` mutation
   pair is gone; the pin lives in the established config-override surface:
   `ModelCapabilityOverride.messageCap` (strict parse with floor 2, yaml
   round-trip, `isEmpty`) under `models.overrides.<provider>.<modelId>`,
   consulted by `_CliMessageCapPolicy.learnedCapFor` via the existing
   `learnedCapOr(learned, pinned)` second tier.
4. **Thread 4 (pathological caps)** — `messageCapTriggerReached` stands
   down when `learnedCap <= margin`; a cap at/below the margin is inside
   the fixed request overhead and `cap − margin` is not a meaningful
   threshold. The reactive heal keeps its own `max(1, cap − margin)` clamp
   (deliberately not shared — the invariant review calls for semantic
   divergence at tiny caps).
5. **Thread 5 (E1 pre-emptive pass)** — `ModelCapsStore` tracks the
   fallback explicitly: a cap-unknown refusal arms exactly one pass
   (in-memory set, never serialized — the persisted `capUnknown` record
   still re-arms the refusal path on the next boot), consumed by both
   compaction gates; a numeric learn disarms it.
6. **Thread 6 (pending flag re-arm safety)** — covered by the symmetric
   arm/consume/disarm design plus the two-dimensional success check: no
   silent re-arm path exists.

The PR description was updated in the same pass (`gh pr edit 1695`): E1
wording, the new verify command, and a "Rework round" section.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — verbatim preservation for split tool
  groups (+ `_displacedResults` helper), E1 pending-pass set on
  `ModelCapsStore` (`isPremptivePassPending`/`takePremptivePass`, disarm on

## Description

Closes #1680
### What changed
gh-1680 adaptive per-model message-cap handling: a provider refusal like `400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048` is now classified (`classifyMessageCapError`), the cap is learned per model in `~/.fah/model-message-caps.json` (`MessageCapPolicy`), and the loop heals once — host compaction pass + payload-only coalesce — then retries exactly once. Once any cap is known, compaction also fires pre-emptively on message count (next-request projection), never letting the session wedge in the first place.

### Key decisions
- **One-shot heal** in the response stream (`agent_loop_message_cap.dart` part): learn → `MessageCapRelief` (host compaction) → arm coalesce → retry once; second refusal is terminal, transcript untouched until relief (AC7: JSONL byte-identical).
- **Coalesce is outbound-only**: `coalesceMessagesForCap` merges whole tool-call/result pairs and old turns older than the newest user message into compact carriers; never drops the running turn or mid-pair blocks.
- **Cap-unknown edge (E1)**: no parseable limit → no coalesce target, relief-only retry.
- **Pre-emptive gate in `AutoCompactor`** rides the existing `CompactionTrigger` slot alongside the token window, so headless gets it for free; CLI wires the policy, relief (structured engine), `/context` caps line, ledger row, and TUI event (emits `compact_phase` + compaction notice, mirrors the over-window relief).
- **Wire**: new `message_cap_repair` event (kind + counts, no text); stream-json filters it as fa-internal; tripwire test extended.

### How to verify

```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[Request refused: 400 array length N exceeds limit M] --> CLS[classifyMessageCapError]
  CLS --> LEARN[MessageCapPolicy.learnFromRefusal → ~/.fah/model-message-caps.json]
  LEARN --> RELIEF[MessageCapRelief: ONE structured compaction]
  LEARN --> COAL[arm coalesce target = cap − margin]
  RELIEF --> RETRY[Retry once]
  COAL --> RETRY
  RETRY -->|refused again| ERR[Terminal error — no loop]
  KNOWN[Cap known] --> GATE[AutoCompactor pre-emptive gate: projected msgs ≥ cap → compact]
```

</details>

### Known pre-existing failures (verified identical on base 096b36d, not regressions)
- `test/integration/headless_log_file_test.dart` (4), `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test.dart` (2), `job_board_stability_pty_test.dart` (1): the sandbox leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` into test children — same failures on base.

{"content":"# PR #1695 rework — review findings addressed

All six open review threads from the PR #1695 pass are fixed in code, each
with a regression test that reproduces the finding first (RED) and passes
after the fix (GREEN).

## Issues/Notes

- No blocking CI failures were present in the input (no `merge_conflicts.md`,
  and `ci_failures.md` only restates known pre-existing sandbox failures that
  reproduce on base). The six open review threads were the rework scope.
- The full-suite run is green; the only failures are the documented
  pre-existing sandbox ones called out in the PR description (verified
  identical on base in earlier passes).
- Thread 4 was fixed as a stand-down (`cap > margin` gate) rather than a
  clamp, per the existing reactive-heal contract — details in the reply and
  the `messageCapTriggerReached` doc comment.

## Approach

For every finding: write the failing scenario test first, watch it fail,
apply the minimal fix, re-run. Then the repo gates: `dart analyze`,
`dart format`, CRAP via `crap4dart` (no touched function above the
threshold; `coalesceMessagesForCap` kept at complexity 17 after extracting
`_displacedResults`), jscpd on `lib/` (0.0% duplicated), and the full test
suite.

1. **Thread 1 (split tool pair across the newest-user cut)** —
   `coalesceMessagesForCap` treated a tool call whose result answers from
   beyond the newest-user message as a mergeable solo unit; the pairing
   repair then dropped the far-side result as an orphan. Now a group that
   hits a non-matching message before every call is answered rides the
   payload **verbatim**: the displaced results are hoisted out of the
   droppable region (or stay in the kept tail for the repair to place back
   next to the call). Content survives in both the cut-probe and the
   mid-region steering interleave shapes.
2. **Thread 2 (token-only success return)** — `_maybeAutoCompact` success
   now requires both dimensions: `after <= _effectiveContextWindow &&
   !overCap`; the message gate is a shared `_messageCapGateReached()`
   helper (known-cap trigger OR the one-shot E1 pass) used by both the loop
   and the boot cap, so no silent re-arm-every-turn path remains.
3. **Thread 3 (unwired pin API)** — the store's `pin`/`remove` mutation
   pair is gone; the pin lives in the established config-override surface:
   `ModelCapabilityOverride.messageCap` (strict parse with floor 2, yaml
   round-trip, `isEmpty`) under `models.overrides.<provider>.<modelId>`,
   consulted by `_CliMessageCapPolicy.learnedCapFor` via the existing
   `learnedCapOr(learned, pinned)` second tier.
4. **Thread 4 (pathological caps)** — `messageCapTriggerReached` stands
   down when `learnedCap <= margin`; a cap at/below the margin is inside
   the fixed request overhead and `cap − margin` is not a meaningful
   threshold. The reactive heal keeps its own `max(1, cap − margin)` clamp
   (deliberately not shared — the invariant review calls for semantic
   divergence at tiny caps).
5. **Thread 5 (E1 pre-emptive pass)** — `ModelCapsStore` tracks the
   fallback explicitly: a cap-unknown refusal arms exactly one pass
   (in-memory set, never serialized — the persisted `capUnknown` record
   still re-arms the refusal path on the next boot), consumed by both
   compaction gates; a numeric learn disarms it.
6. **Thread 6 (pending flag re-arm safety)** — covered by the symmetric
   arm/consume/disarm design plus the two-dimensional success check: no
   silent re-arm path exists.

The PR description was updated in the same pass (`gh pr edit 1695`): E1
wording, the new verify command, and a "Rework round" section.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — verbatim preservation for split tool
  groups (+ `_displacedResults` helper), E1 pending-pass set on
  `ModelCapsStore` (`isPremptivePassPending`/`takePremptivePass`, disarm on
  numeric learn, no pin/remove mutation pair), `cap > margin` stand-down in

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` — shared `_messageCapGateReached()`

  `ModelCapabilityOverride.messageCap` field with strict parse/validate and

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` — `_CliMessageCapPolicy.learnedCapFor`

- `test/cli/agent_cli_message_cap_test.dart` — new file, 10 tests (E1

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `coalesceMessagesForCap` no longer
treats a tool call whose result answers from beyond the newest-user cut as a

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `messageCapTriggerReached` stands
down when `learnedCap <= margin`: the guard is now
`learnedCap != null && learnedCap > margin && messageCount >= learnedCap - margin`.

A cap at or below the margin is inside the fixed request overhead, `cap −
margin` is not a meaningful pre-emptive threshold, and an always-true trigger
would have wedged the session into a compact-every-turn state.

Deliberately NOT clamped: the reactive heal keeps its own
`max(1, cap − margin)` target per refusal — a tiny cap still converges to a
workable outbound shape there; only the pre-emptive gate disarms.

Regression tests in `test/agent/message_cap_store_test.dart`: caps 1, 3, and 10
(default margin) never trigger regardless of count; cap 11 arms exactly at the
boundary; a custom margin re-arms a cap that exceeds it.

## PR Description

### What changed
gh-1680 adaptive per-model message-cap handling: a provider refusal like `400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048` is now classified (`classifyMessageCapError`), the cap is learned per model in `~/.fah/model-message-caps.json` (`MessageCapPolicy`), and the loop heals once — host compaction pass + payload-only coalesce — then retries exactly once. Once any cap is known, compaction also fires pre-emptively on message count (next-request projection), never letting the session wedge in the first place.

### Key decisions

- **Cap-unknown edge (E1)**: no parseable limit → no coalesce target, relief-only retry.
- **Pre-emptive gate in `AutoCompactor`** rides the existing `CompactionTrigger` slot alongside the token window, so headless gets it for free; CLI wires the policy, relief (structured engine), `/context` caps line, ledger row, and TUI event (emits `compact_phase` + compaction notice, mirrors the over-window relief).
- **Wire**: new `message_cap_repair` event (kind + counts, no text); stream-json filters it as fa-internal; tripwire test extended.

# pr-1695: gh-1680 [GOAL] Adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, pre-emptive compaction before the cap (dmtools-factory 01a14b3a wedge no hardcoded provider tables)

## Description

Closes #1680
### What changed
gh-1680 adaptive per-model message-cap handling: a provider refusal like `400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048` is now classified (`classifyMessageCapError`), the cap is learned per model in `~/.fah/model-message-caps.json` (`MessageCapPolicy`), and the loop heals once — host compaction pass + payload-only coalesce — then retries exactly once. Once any cap is known, compaction also fires pre-emptively on message count (next-request projection), never letting the session wedge in the first place.

### Key decisions
- **One-shot heal** in the response stream (`agent_loop_message_cap.dart` part): learn → `MessageCapRelief` (host compaction) → arm coalesce → retry once; second refusal is terminal, transcript untouched until relief (AC7: JSONL byte-identical).
- **Coalesce is outbound-only**: `coalesceMessagesForCap` merges whole tool-call/result pairs and old turns older than the newest user message into compact carriers; never drops the running turn or mid-pair blocks.
- **Cap-unknown edge (E1)**: no parseable limit → no coalesce target, relief-only retry.
- **Pre-emptive gate in `AutoCompactor`** rides the existing `CompactionTrigger` slot alongside the token window, so headless gets it for free; CLI wires the policy, relief (structured engine), `/context` caps line, ledger row, and TUI event (emits `compact_phase` + compaction notice, mirrors the over-window relief).
- **Wire**: new `message_cap_repair` event (kind + counts, no text); stream-json filters it as fa-internal; tripwire test extended.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_store_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_compactor_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_source_scan_test.dart test/overflow_test.dart
```

<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[Request refused: 400 array length N exceeds limit M] --> CLS[classifyMessageCapError]
  CLS --> LEARN[MessageCapPolicy.learnFromRefusal → ~/.fah/model-message-caps.json]
  LEARN --> RELIEF[MessageCapRelief: ONE structured compaction]
  LEARN --> COAL[arm coalesce target = cap − margin]
  RELIEF --> RETRY[Retry once]
  COAL --> RETRY
  RETRY -->|refused again| ERR[Terminal error — no loop]
  KNOWN[Cap known] --> GATE[AutoCompactor pre-emptive gate: projected msgs ≥ cap → compact]
```

{"content":"# PR #1695 rework — review findings addressed

All six open review threads from the PR #1695 pass are fixed in code, each
with a regression test that reproduces the finding first (RED) and passes
after the fix (GREEN).

## Issues/Notes

- No blocking CI failures were present in the input (no `merge_conflicts.md`,
  and `ci_failures.md` only restates known pre-existing sandbox failures that
  reproduce on base). The six open review threads were the rework scope.
- The full-suite run is green; the only failures are the documented
  pre-existing sandbox ones called out in the PR description (verified
  identical on base in earlier passes).
- Thread 4 was fixed as a stand-down (`cap > margin` gate) rather than a
  clamp, per the existing reactive-heal contract — details in the reply and
  the `messageCapTriggerReached` doc comment.

## Approach

For every finding: write the failing scenario test first, watch it fail,
apply the minimal fix, re-run. Then the repo gates: `dart analyze`,
`dart format`, CRAP via `crap4dart` (no touched function above the
threshold; `coalesceMessagesForCap` kept at complexity 17 after extracting
`_displacedResults`), jscpd on `lib/` (0.0% duplicated), and the full test
suite.

1. **Thread 1 (split tool pair across the newest-user cut)** —
   `coalesceMessagesForCap` treated a tool call whose result answers from
   beyond the newest-user message as a mergeable solo unit; the pairing
   repair then dropped the far-side result as an orphan. Now a group that
   hits a non-matching message before every call is answered rides the
   payload **verbatim**: the displaced results are hoisted out of the
   droppable region (or stay in the kept tail for the repair to place back
   next to the call). Content survives in both the cut-probe and the
   mid-region steering interleave shapes.
2. **Thread 2 (token-only success return)** — `_maybeAutoCompact` success
   now requires both dimensions: `after <= _effectiveContextWindow &&
   !overCap`; the message gate is a shared `_messageCapGateReached()`
   helper (known-cap trigger OR the one-shot E1 pass) used by both the loop
   and the boot cap, so no silent re-arm-every-turn path remains.
3. **Thread 3 (unwired pin API)** — the store's `pin`/`remove` mutation
   pair is gone; the pin lives in the established config-override surface:
   `ModelCapabilityOverride.messageCap` (strict parse with floor 2, yaml
   round-trip, `isEmpty`) under `models.overrides.<provider>.<modelId>`,
   consulted by `_CliMessageCapPolicy.learnedCapFor` via the existing
   `learnedCapOr(learned, pinned)` second tier.
4. **Thread 4 (pathological caps)** — `messageCapTriggerReached` stands
   down when `learnedCap <= margin`; a cap at/below the margin is inside
   the fixed request overhead and `cap − margin` is not a meaningful
   threshold. The reactive heal keeps its own `max(1, cap − margin)` clamp
   (deliberately not shared — the invariant review calls for semantic
   divergence at tiny caps).
5. **Thread 5 (E1 pre-emptive pass)** — `ModelCapsStore` tracks the
   fallback explicitly: a cap-unknown refusal arms exactly one pass
   (in-memory set, never serialized — the persisted `capUnknown` record
   still re-arms the refusal path on the next boot), consumed by both
   compaction gates; a numeric learn disarms it.
6. **Thread 6 (pending flag re-arm safety)** — covered by the symmetric
   arm/consume/disarm design plus the two-dimensional success check: no
   silent re-arm path exists.

The PR description was updated in the same pass (`gh pr edit 1695`): E1
wording, the new verify command, and a "Rework round" section.

- `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — verbatim preservation for split tool
  groups (+ `_displacedResults` helper), E1 pending-pass set on
  `ModelCapsStore` (`isPremptivePassPending`/`takePremptivePass`, disarm on
  numeric learn, no pin/remove mutation pair), `cap > margin` stand-down in

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `coalesceMessagesForCap` no longer
treats a tool call whose result answers from beyond the newest-user cut as a
mergeable solo unit. When the pairing scan hits a non-matching message before
every call is answered, the whole group rides the payload **verbatim** (the
displaced results are hoisted out of the droppable region, and the pairing
repair places any far-side tail result back next to its call). The old behavior
merged the call into a `[coalesced …]` carrier, so the repair pass dropped the
far-side result as an orphan and the tool output silently disappeared.

Regression tests in `test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart`:

- **cut probe** — `[call c1, user steer, result c1]` with `target=2`: the call
  stays verbatim and the result survives with its content intact (previously
  dropped; only a synthesized placeholder remained).
- **mid-region interleave** — `[user older, call c1, user steer, result c1,
  user newest]`: the pair stays verbatim too.

  clamp, per the existing reactive-heal contract — details in the reply and
  the `messageCapTriggerReached` doc comment.

## Approach

For every finding: write the failing scenario test first, watch it fail,
apply the minimal fix, re-run. Then the repo gates: `dart analyze`,
`dart format`, CRAP via `crap4dart` (no touched function above the
threshold; `coalesceMessagesForCap` kept at complexity 17 after extracting
`_displacedResults`), jscpd on `lib/` (0.0% duplicated), and the full test
suite.

1. **Thread 1 (split tool pair across the newest-user cut)** —
   `coalesceMessagesForCap` treated a tool call whose result answers from
   beyond the newest-user message as a mergeable solo unit; the pairing
   repair then dropped the far-side result as an orphan. Now a group that
   hits a non-matching message before every call is answered rides the
   payload **verbatim**: the displaced results are hoisted out of the
   droppable region (or stay in the kept tail for the repair to place back
   next to the call). Content survives in both the cut-probe and the
   mid-region steering interleave shapes.
2. **Thread 2 (token-only success return)** — `_maybeAutoCompact` success
   now requires both dimensions: `after <= _effectiveContextWindow &&
   !overCap`; the message gate is a shared `_messageCapGateReached()`
   helper (known-cap trigger OR the one-shot E1 pass) used by both the loop
   and the boot cap, so no silent re-arm-every-turn path remains.
3. **Thread 3 (unwired pin API)** — the store's `pin`/`remove` mutation
   pair is gone; the pin lives in the established config-override surface:
   `ModelCapabilityOverride.messageCap` (strict parse with floor 2, yaml
   round-trip, `isEmpty`) under `models.overrides.<provider>.<modelId>`,
   consulted by `_CliMessageCapPolicy.learnedCapFor` via the existing
   `learnedCapOr(learned, pinned)` second tier.
4. **Thread 4 (pathological caps)** — `messageCapTriggerReached` stands
   down when `learnedCap <= margin`; a cap at/below the margin is inside
   the fixed request overhead and `cap − margin` is not a meaningful
   threshold. The reactive heal keeps its own `max(1, cap − margin)` clamp
   (deliberately not shared — the invariant review calls for semantic
   divergence at tiny caps).
5. **Thread 5 (E1 pre-emptive pass)** — `ModelCapsStore` tracks the
   fallback explicitly: a cap-unknown refusal arms exactly one pass
   (in-memory set, never serialized — the persisted `capUnknown` record
   still re-arms the refusal path on the next boot), consumed by both
   compaction gates; a numeric learn disarms it.
6. **Thread 6 (pending flag re-arm safety)** — covered by the symmetric
   arm/consume/disarm design plus the two-dimensional success check: no
   silent re-arm path exists.

The PR description was updated in the same pass (`gh pr edit 1695`): E1
wording, the new verify command, and a "Rework round" section.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — verbatim preservation for split tool
  groups (+ `_displacedResults` helper), E1 pending-pass set on
  `ModelCapsStore` (`isPremptivePassPending`/`takePremptivePass`, disarm on
  numeric learn, no pin/remove mutation pair), `cap > margin` stand-down in
  `messageCapTriggerReached`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` — shared `_messageCapGateReached()`

- `lib/src/model_roles/capability_resolver.dart` —

{"content":"# PR #1695 rework — review findings addressed

All six open review threads from the PR #1695 pass are fixed in code, each
with a regression test that reproduces the finding first (RED) and passes
after the fix (GREEN).

## Issues/Notes

- No blocking CI failures were present in the input (no `merge_conflicts.md`,
  and `ci_failures.md` only restates known pre-existing sandbox failures that
  reproduce on base). The six open review threads were the rework scope.
- The full-suite run is green; the only failures are the documented
  pre-existing sandbox ones called out in the PR description (verified
  identical on base in earlier passes).
- Thread 4 was fixed as a stand-down (`cap > margin` gate) rather than a
  clamp, per the existing reactive-heal contract — details in the reply and
  the `messageCapTriggerReached` doc comment.

## Approach

For every finding: write the failing scenario test first, watch it fail,
apply the minimal fix, re-run. Then the repo gates: `dart analyze`,
`dart format`, CRAP via `crap4dart` (no touched function above the
threshold; `coalesceMessagesForCap` kept at complexity 17 after extracting
`_displacedResults`), jscpd on `lib/` (0.0% duplicated), and the full test
suite.

1. **Thread 1 (split tool pair across the newest-user cut)** —
   `coalesceMessagesForCap` treated a tool call whose result answers from
   beyond the newest-user message as a mergeable solo unit; the pairing
   repair then dropped the far-side result as an orphan. Now a group that
   hits a non-matching message before every call is answered rides the
   payload **verbatim**: the displaced results are hoisted out of the
   droppable region (or stay in the kept tail for the repair to place back
   next to the call). Content survives in both the cut-probe and the
   mid-region steering interleave shapes.
2. **Thread 2 (token-only success return)** — `_maybeAutoCompact` success
   now requires both dimensions: `after <= _effectiveContextWindow &&
   !overCap`; the message gate is a shared `_messageCapGateReached()`
   helper (known-cap trigger OR the one-shot E1 pass) used by both the loop
   and the boot cap, so no silent re-arm-every-turn path remains.
3. **Thread 3 (unwired pin API)** — the store's `pin`/`remove` mutation
   pair is gone; the pin lives in the established config-override surface:
   `ModelCapabilityOverride.messageCap` (strict parse with floor 2, yaml
   round-trip, `isEmpty`) under `models.overrides.<provider>.<modelId>`,
   consulted by `_CliMessageCapPolicy.learnedCapFor` via the existing
   `learnedCapOr(learned, pinned)` second tier.
4. **Thread 4 (pathological caps)** — `messageCapTriggerReached` stands
   down when `learnedCap <= margin`; a cap at/below the margin is inside
   the fixed request overhead and `cap − margin` is not a meaningful
   threshold. The reactive heal keeps its own `max(1, cap − margin)` clamp
   (deliberately not shared — the invariant review calls for semantic
   divergence at tiny caps).
5. **Thread 5 (E1 pre-emptive pass)** — `ModelCapsStore` tracks the
   fallback explicitly: a cap-unknown refusal arms exactly one pass
   (in-memory set, never serialized — the persisted `capUnknown` record
   still re-arms the refusal path on the next boot), consumed by both
   compaction gates; a numeric learn disarms it.
6. **Thread 6 (pending flag re-arm safety)** — covered by the symmetric
   arm/consume/disarm design plus the two-dimensional success check: no
   silent re-arm path exists.

The PR description was updated in the same pass (`gh pr edit 1695`): E1
wording, the new verify command, and a "Rework round" section.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — verbatim preservation for split tool
  groups (+ `_displacedResults` helper), E1 pending-pass set on
  `ModelCapsStore` (`isPremptivePassPending`/`takePremptivePass`, disarm on

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` — shared `_messageCapGateReached()`

  `ModelCapabilityOverride.messageCap` field with strict parse/validate and

- `test/cli/agent_cli_message_cap_test.dart` — new file, 10 tests (E1

{"content":"# PR #1695 rework — review findings addressed

All six open review threads from the PR #1695 pass are fixed in code, each
with a regression test that reproduces the finding first (RED) and passes
after the fix (GREEN).

## Issues/Notes

- No blocking CI failures were present in the input (no `merge_conflicts.md`,
  and `ci_failures.md` only restates known pre-existing sandbox failures that
  reproduce on base). The six open review threads were the rework scope.
- The full-suite run is green; the only failures are the documented
  pre-existing sandbox ones called out in the PR description (verified
  identical on base in earlier passes).
- Thread 4 was fixed as a stand-down (`cap > margin` gate) rather than a
  clamp, per the existing reactive-heal contract — details in the reply and
  the `messageCapTriggerReached` doc comment.

## Approach

For every finding: write the failing scenario test first, watch it fail,
apply the minimal fix, re-run. Then the repo gates: `dart analyze`,
`dart format`, CRAP via `crap4dart` (no touched function above the
threshold; `coalesceMessagesForCap` kept at complexity 17 after extracting
`_displacedResults`), jscpd on `lib/` (0.0% duplicated), and the full test
suite.

1. **Thread 1 (split tool pair across the newest-user cut)** —
   `coalesceMessagesForCap` treated a tool call whose result answers from
   beyond the newest-user message as a mergeable solo unit; the pairing
   repair then dropped the far-side result as an orphan. Now a group that
   hits a non-matching message before every call is answered rides the
   payload **verbatim**: the displaced results are hoisted out of the
   droppable region (or stay in the kept tail for the repair to place back
   next to the call). Content survives in both the cut-probe and the
   mid-region steering interleave shapes.
2. **Thread 2 (token-only success return)** — `_maybeAutoCompact` success
   now requires both dimensions: `after <= _effectiveContextWindow &&
   !overCap`; the message gate is a shared `_messageCapGateReached()`
   helper (known-cap trigger OR the one-shot E1 pass) used by both the loop
   and the boot cap, so no silent re-arm-every-turn path remains.
3. **Thread 3 (unwired pin API)** — the store's `pin`/`remove` mutation
   pair is gone; the pin lives in the established config-override surface:
   `ModelCapabilityOverride.messageCap` (strict parse with floor 2, yaml
   round-trip, `isEmpty`) under `models.overrides.<provider>.<modelId>`,
   consulted by `_CliMessageCapPolicy.learnedCapFor` via the existing
   `learnedCapOr(learned, pinned)` second tier.
4. **Thread 4 (pathological caps)** — `messageCapTriggerReached` stands
   down when `learnedCap <= margin`; a cap at/below the margin is inside
   the fixed request overhead and `cap − margin` is not a meaningful
   threshold. The reactive heal keeps its own `max(1, cap − margin)` clamp
   (deliberately not shared — the invariant review calls for semantic
   divergence at tiny caps).
5. **Thread 5 (E1 pre-emptive pass)** — `ModelCapsStore` tracks the
   fallback explicitly: a cap-unknown refusal arms exactly one pass
   (in-memory set, never serialized — the persisted `capUnknown` record
   still re-arms the refusal path on the next boot), consumed by both
   compaction gates; a numeric learn disarms it.
6. **Thread 6 (pending flag re-arm safety)** — covered by the symmetric
   arm/consume/disarm design plus the two-dimensional success check: no
   silent re-arm path exists.

The PR description was updated in the same pass (`gh pr edit 1695`): E1
wording, the new verify command, and a "Rework round" section.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — verbatim preservation for split tool
  groups (+ `_displacedResults` helper), E1 pending-pass set on
  `ModelCapsStore` (`isPremptivePassPending`/`takePremptivePass`, disarm on
  numeric learn, no pin/remove mutation pair), `cap > margin` stand-down in
  `messageCapTriggerReached`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` — shared `_messageCapGateReached()`
  gate in `_maybeAutoCompact` and `_capResumedContext`; success requires
  `!overCap` too.
- `lib/src/model_roles/capability_resolver.dart` —
  `ModelCapabilityOverride.messageCap` field with strict parse/validate and
  yaml round-trip.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` — `_CliMessageCapPolicy.learnedCapFor`

- `test/cli/agent_cli_message_cap_test.dart` — new file, 10 tests (E1

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/agent/message_cap.dart` — `coalesceMessagesForCap` no longer
treats a tool call whose result answers from beyond the newest-user cut as a
mergeable solo unit. When the pairing scan hits a non-matching message before
every call is answered, the whole group rides the payload **verbatim** (the
displaced results are hoisted out of the droppable region, and the pairing
repair places any far-side tail result back next to its call). The old behavior
merged the call into a `[coalesced …]` carrier, so the repair pass dropped the
far-side result as an orphan and the tool output silently disappeared.

- **mid-region interleave** — `[user older, call c1, user steer, result c1,
  user newest]`: the pair stays verbatim too.

down when `learnedCap <= margin`: the guard is now

- Both compaction gates (`_maybeAutoCompact` and `_capResumedContext` in

  next request compacts pre-emptively instead of walking into the 400 the
